title: Aditya-L1: India's Sun Watcher

segments.say: Point a telescope at the Sun from Earth, and our air gets in the way. So India sent one a million and a half kilometres out.
Aditya-L1 lifted off on a PSLV from Sriharikota on the second of September, twenty twenty-three.

anim.title: What is L1?
items: A balance point between Earth and Sun
The Sun never goes out of view

segments.say: Its home is L1, a point where the pulls of the Earth and the Sun balance. From there, the Sun is never hidden, not by night, not by an eclipse.

items.label: Measure particles and fields at L1

segments.say: It carries seven instruments. Four look straight at the Sun. Three measure the particles and magnetic fields that stream past.
It reached its orbit around L1 on the sixth of January, twenty twenty-four, and has been sending pictures of the Sun's surface since.
Why bother? Storms on the Sun can damage satellites, radio links and power grids. Watching them early gives us time to prepare.

anim.title: For your answer
items: India's first space mission to study the Sun

segments.say: For GS Three: India's first solar mission, parked at L1, studying the Sun's outer layers and space weather.

sources: ISRO, Aditya-L1 mission page: launched 2 September 2023 on PSLV-C57 from SDSC SHAR; first Indian space-based mission to study the Sun; placed in a halo orbit around L1, about 1.5 million km from Earth; seven payloads, four remote-sensing and three in-situ
ISRO press release, 6 January 2024: Aditya-L1 inserted into its halo orbit around L1
PIB releases on Aditya-L1: objectives include coronal heating, solar wind and space weather

quiz.q: About how far from Earth is L1?
quiz.why: L1 is about 1.5 million km away, about 1% of the way to the Sun.

quiz.q: Why is L1 a good place to watch the Sun?
options: The Sun is never blocked from view
It is inside the Sun's corona
quiz.why: No night and no eclipse block the view from L1.

quiz.q: How many instruments does Aditya-L1 carry?
quiz.why: Seven: four looking at the Sun, three measuring particles and fields.

reviewNote: Facts were read against ISRO's Aditya-L1 page and press releases. Pictures are ISRO's own. Moving facts: mission status and data releases change over time.
